text:
sasha: FYI VectorOps SI hit a showstopper during their production cutover for NexisHealth this morning. They reported both image verification failures and a GPU driver probe error. Can partnerships + marketplace help triage?
lee: What's the exact failure payload?
sasha: From the SI: installer exits with "verification failed: signature mismatch" when pulling our marketplace image, and then when they used a locally rebuilt image the runtime fails on GPU probe: `gpu_probe: unknown vermagic`
marco: Signature mismatch first suggests they didn't pull by digest, or the marketplace signing key rotated and their client cache is stale.
alyssa: I asked them to run `docker inspect --format='{{.RepoDigests}}' redwood/edge:latest` and `cosign verify` output. They returned the tag only, no digest, and cosign failed with `public key not found`.
lee: Are we in the middle of a key rotation? @marketplace-build any rolling key updates today?
marketplace-build: Not scheduled today. We pushed an image yesterday but signing key remained the same. Could be SI environment blocking cosign or missing root certs.
marco: For the GPU vermagic: sounds like a module/driver built against different kernel headers. SI mentioned they run a FIPS-compliant kernel and backport patches. That often changes vermagic.
sasha: VectorOps wants a clear step-by-step to recover quickly: 1) get app back online, 2) ensure image integrity, 3) document for future SI installs.
alyssa: Recovery options: - If signature is failing due to missing cosign key, we can provide a signed digest URL they can curl/download, or they can pull by sha (recommended). - For GPU, short term fallback is to switch inference to hosted endpoints until drivers are reconciled.
lee: Need to coordinate with HW partner too — some of their GPUs require a vendor driver package with matching kernel ABI. @hw-partner-bot any notes?
hw-partner-bot: [hw-partner-bot] Known issue: vendor-drivers v2.1.4 require kernel-5.10+ with unpatched vermagic. For FIPS-patched kernels, vendor recommends building driver from source with DKMS.
marco: DKMS build is doable but risky during cutover. Alternative: rebase to our signed marketplace digest (if their compliance team allows) and use our prebuilt driver combo.
sasha: VectorOps says compliance prohibits using unapproved images without their audit. They rebuilt image locally to add compliance agents, which likely broke the signature and maybe changed kernel headers.
alyssa: Action items: 1) I will send VectorOps a signed digest link and a cli snippet for pulling by sha with verification. 2) Marco will write up a short driver-rebuild and DKMS checklist we can hand to SI. 3) Marketplace-build to confirm the digest and provide the cosign public key + root cert bundle. 4) I'll work with infra/security to provision a temporary hosted-inference allowlist so NexisHealth traffic can route to Redwood-hosted endpoints while they resolve.
lee: Please include explicit commands. VectorOps is not super fluent on cosign.
alyssa: Commands I will send:
```
# pull by digest and verify
docker pull redwood/edge@sha256:<digest>
cosign verify --key ./redwood_pub.key redwood/edge@sha256:<digest>
# quick check for docker digests
docker inspect --format='{{.RepoDigests}}' redwood/edge:3.9.0
# DKMS build (example)
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y dkms build-essential linux-headers-$(uname -r)
sudo dkms add -m nvidia -v 525.105.17
sudo dkms build -m nvidia -v 525.105.17
sudo dkms install -m nvidia -v 525.105.17
```
marco: Also add these diagnostics for the SDK/agent so we can correlate traces: `RW_TRACE_ID` env, `redwood-agent --dump-config`, and full `dmesg` around the probe.
sasha: VectorOps forgot RW_TRACE_ID in their original upload. I've asked them to rerun and include it.
marketplace-build: I've pasted the public cosign key into the secure SI folder and created a signed digest URL: https://marketplace.redwood.com/signed/redwood-edge-3.9.0.sha256 (signed, TTL 48h). Also verifying the image build matrix for 3.9.0 — the published driver bundle is nvidia-525 built against kernel 5.15 base.
lee: Good. For the short-term hosted fallback, security needs to confirm data flow is permitted for NexisHealth. Alyssa, loop security and provide the traffic window.
alyssa: On it. I'll open a short approval ticket and post the ticket id here. Meanwhile VectorOps will attempt a DKMS build; they estimate 90 minutes. They also asked if we can provide a minimal 'audit patch' guide so they can add compliance agents without rebuilding driver stack.
marco: We'll draft a small diff-based guidance: add agents post-boot as systemd units rather than baking into the kernel/module build. That reduces risk.
sasha: Timeline: VectorOps will try DKMS now (~90m); if unsuccessful, they'll pivot to pulling our signed digest and requesting an expedited compliance sign-off to use our image for the cutover. We'll reconvene in this thread with updates. Thanks all. :shipit:
